title: Researchers Discover 253 Security Vulnerabilities Across 343 AI Agent Tools in MCP Servers
key_facts: Researchers identified 253 verified security vulnerabilities affecting 343 AI agent tools across 118 Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.
The evaluation covered 273 open-source MCP servers containing 3,405 tools, using a new fuzzing framework called ToFu.

The study, "ToFu: Exploiting and Fuzzing the LLM-Orchestrator-Tool Trust Boundary", was published on arXiv on 9 Oct 2026 by researchers from Pennsylvania State University, Universite Montpellier and Dartmouth College.
Issues include arbitrary path traversal, log injection, data exfiltration and command bypass.

The "Repeat-After-Me" attack makes a model reproduce text that the orchestration layer then runs as a real tool call; it was replicated across six frameworks including LangGraph, Microsoft MAF, Google ADK 2.0, AutoGen, AWS Strands and CrewAI.
Tool descriptions often do not match actual code; prompt filtering and better model behaviour cannot replace security checks in the software that performs file, network or command operations.
The study focuses on tool-level contract violations, not on confirming exploitation of every affected deployment; the figures use different measurement units.
quote_evidence: Researchers have identified 253 verified security vulnerabilities affecting 343 AI agent tools across 118 Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.
The findings are based on an evaluation of 273 open-source MCP servers containing 3,405 tools, using a new fuzzing framework called ToFu.
The study focuses on tool-level contract violations rather than confirming the exploitation of every affected deployment.
why_it_matters_hint: Many open-source connectors that let AI agents use software tools accept unsafe inputs from the model, so tool code must treat model output as untrusted.
event_date: Study posted on arXiv 9 Oct 2026; article published 13 Oct 2026
notes: Academic preprint reported four days after posting; no peer review mentioned; older than the window start, so re-dated as a follow-up and scored one point lower.
